A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WUSH research and contain readable main text, algorithms, equations, figures, tables, and theoretical and experimental appendices. Content can be reliably matched despite extensive reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports original layerwise quantization losses, LLM benchmark accuracy, KL divergence, and GPU throughput measurements, including appendix results.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results and adds calibration-dataset sensitivity, RMS-profile comparisons, and preprocessing and storage measurements.

M1.justification: The defining WUSH transform remains, but its reported preprocessing procedure changes substantially. V2 Algorithm 1 uses a global Cholesky factor, residual-output updates, and reverse block traversal. V3 Algorithms 1–2 specify independent blockwise RTN, trace-scaled damping, and forward GPTQ processing using a Cholesky factor of the inverse Hessian. The PDFs do not establish that retained accuracy experiments were rerun with this revised procedure.

E1.justification: V3 Table 5 adds Open-Platypus calibration and evaluates C4 as a calibration source alongside FineWeb. V2 already used C4 for KL-divergence evaluation. The downstream benchmarks, model families, and quantization formats are retained.

E2.justification: The existing accuracy and layerwise-loss comparator sets remain unchanged. New Figure 5 evaluates RMS equalization against identity, random rotation, Hadamard, WUS, and SmoothQuant; SmoothQuant now participates in this diagnostic comparison, beyond its existing accuracy comparison in Table 2.

E3.justification: V3 introduces a calibration-source comparison for Qwen3-8B/MXFP4 and profiles the RTN calibration/transform-construction pipeline using time and GPU memory on H100/B200 hardware. It also measures checkpoint storage overhead. Existing layerwise-loss and RTX 5090 throughput settings remain; expanded group-size explanations do not establish changed settings.

E4.justification: Supplementary investigation expands beyond the retained component-loss ablations. Table 5 tests dependence on calibration data, Figure 5 examines joint weight/activation RMS equalization, and Appendix B.2 investigates preprocessing and storage costs. These address new questions about calibration robustness, mechanism, and practical overhead.

E5.justification: V3 expands Figure 3's caption to identify the existing variability display as standard deviations. V2 already included those plots, standard-deviation descriptions for appendix figures, multiple-seed aggregation, and ten-run random-rotation averaging. No increased run count or new statistical test is reported.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes NVFP4 GPTQ-I GSM8K from 82.60 to 81.25, making it consistent with the retained 75.72 average. Table 1, the matched appendix accuracy/KL tables, and Platinum heatmap values are unchanged. V3 adds calibration-sensitivity, RMS-profile, and resource results, including model-specific preprocessing measurements of 9–38 minutes and 10–40 GB.

T1.justification: The original FP/INT optimality theorem and supporting proofs are retained. New Appendix A.3 derives the transformed second moment HSH-transpose and its constant diagonal, establishing blockwise RMS equalization. Section 3 also adds computational-complexity and storage-overhead derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction revise the maximum WUSH speedup from 6.6× to 5.8×. Section 5 distinguishes FP4 matrix multiplication alone from execution including transformation and quantization. The core optimality contribution and headline accuracy gains remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V3 explicitly distinguishes the stochastic theoretical surrogate from deterministic RTN experiments, explains WUS's INT4 failure through coordinate amplification, and discusses RMS balancing and calibration stability. It qualifies preprocessing costs as implementation-dependent. The earlier future-work suggestion of diagonal approximations is removed.

D1.justification: V3 provides explicit block-construction and damping pseudocode, 16-bit transform-storage assumptions, and per-model preprocessing hardware, runtime, memory, and storage information. Appendix B.2 explains the offloading/recomputation tradeoff. The source-code access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited-work set is retained; the Chen and Egiazarian publication updates do not introduce new works. Positioning is refined by contrasting WUSH with iterative calibration-time transform optimization in SpinQuant/FlatQuant and by distinguishing its RMS balancing from SmoothQuant's diagonal rescaling.

P1.justification: V3 condenses the introduction by removing a repeated transform equation, revises kernel/results explanations, removes the Future Work section, adds funding and impact text, and introduces appendix subsections. Most existing exposition and proof prose remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout, substantially resizing and relocating displays. Appendix accuracy figures switch from stacked to side-by-side arrangements. V3 adds Figure 5 and Tables 5–7, replaces one algorithm display with two, reorders existing tables, and expands legends and captions.

improvement.justification: V3 improves accuracy and transparency by separating the 5.8× complete inference speedup from the 6.6× MatMul-only result and correcting Table 2's inconsistent entry. Calibration-sensitivity checks, RMS analysis, and measured preprocessing/storage costs provide useful additional support. The principal theorem and most benchmark evidence remain unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
